title: Slide 1 · Ontologies and knowledge graphs
question: Ava requested C2. C1 is available. A rule needs both a request and availability for the same item. Which additional availability fact would complete this case?
answer: Available(C2) would match the item in Ava’s request. C1’s availability answers a question about a different camera.

title: Slide 2 · Read a fact as an edge
question: Which triple would record that C1 is stored in Cabinet7?
answer: Use (C1, storedIn, Cabinet7). The edge starts at the item and ends at the place where it is stored.

title: Slide 3 · Distinguish an item from a class
question: The desk moves C1 to a different cabinet. What type edge should change?
answer: None for that move. C1 is still a Camera. Its location edge is the one affected.

title: Slide 4 · Let a class carry meaning
question: If all you know is that item E7 is Equipment, can this hierarchy tell you it is a Camera?
answer: No. Camera membership implies Equipment membership. Equipment can also contain tripods or other kinds of item.

title: Slide 5 · Follow a path with a shared node
question: Suppose the location for C1 is missing but Cabinet2 is recorded for C2. What can the path answer?
answer: It still identifies Ava’s requested item as C1. It supplies no location for that item. The edge from C2 cannot complete a path through C1.

title: Slide 6 · Use the camera as the link between two records
question: Replace this line: requests = [("Ava", "C1")] with: requests = [("Ava", "C2")] What will print?
answer:
Ava C2 Cabinet2
The request now supplies C2 as the lookup key. The location dictionary already maps C2 to Cabinet2.

title: Slide 8 · From this module to the next
question: A clerk labels a new C3 as equipment after reading its Camera type. A reviewer asks where “equipment” came from. Which two pieces should the clerk show?
answer: Show the record that C3 is a Camera and the statement that every Camera is Equipment. Together they explain how the individual received the broader type.

title: Office hours · Is the knowledge graph the same thing as the ontology?
question: Is the knowledge graph the same thing as the ontology?
answer: The lending graph can record Ava’s request and C1’s location. The ontology supplies terms such as Camera and Equipment and a statement connecting their meanings. A system may store both kinds of statements in the same graph. Together they let you ask both what the desk recorded about this item and what follows from its category.

title: Office hours · If I draw an edge between two nodes, does the reverse edge hold too?
question: If I draw an edge between two nodes, does the reverse edge hold too?
answer: Read the edge label in its declared direction. From Ava requested C1 you can look backward to find who requested C1. That operation still answers the original relationship. Claiming that C1 requested Ava would introduce a different statement.

title: Exercise 1
question: Encode “Ava requested C1, a camera stored in Cabinet7” as three triples.
answer: (Ava, requested, C1), (C1, type, Camera), and (C1, storedIn, Cabinet7). Reusing C1 allows another query to connect the three facts.

title: Exercise 2
question: The inventory adds a projector P3 without linking the Projector class to Equipment. Which general statement would support the inference that any projector is equipment?
answer: Record Projector as a subclass of Equipment. From P3 has type Projector, the class rule then yields P3 has type Equipment.

title: Exercise 3
question: Design a graph query that returns everyone who requested an item stored in Cabinet7. Which name has to match twice?
answer: Match (person, requested, item) and (item, storedIn, Cabinet7). The same item fills the end of the first edge and the start of the second. Return the matching person.

title: Lab case 1 · One class step
question: Which type for C1 follows by the subclass rule?
answer: C1 has type Equipment. The rule applies to individual members of Camera, and C1 is one of them.

title: Lab case 2 · A longer hierarchy
question: What extra work is needed to reach Equipment for C1?
answer: Apply the membership rule twice. The first application gives C1 type Camera. That newly inferred type supplies the starting point for the second application, which gives C1 type Equipment.

title: Lab case 3 · A broken path
question: For whose request can staff find the item’s storage cabinet?
answer: Bo’s path runs through C2 to Cabinet2. Ava’s reaches C1 and stops. A storedIn edge beginning at C1 would let the desk answer her location question.
